pharm: GI prokinetic / serotonergic agonist for IBS-C
quick: IBS-C: 6 mg orally twice daily before meals (women <65 yr without CV risk)
Limited data; use only if clearly needed
Excreted in milk in animals; avoid / caution
No dose adjustment in mild-moderate; not recommended in severe renal impairment
Not recommended in moderate-severe hepatic impairment; avoid
Cardiovascular/ischemic symptoms; diarrhea; signs of ischemic colitis
summary: Tegaserod is a 5-HT4 serotonin receptor agonist that stimulates gut motility and secretion, indicated for irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) in adult WOMEN younger than 65 years who do NOT have a history of cardiovascular ischemic events. It was withdrawn in 2007 over cardiovascular safety concerns and reintroduced (Zelnorm) by the FDA in 2019 with a restricted, lower-risk population. Contraindicated in patients with cardiovascular ischemic disease, ischemic colitis, or severe hepatic/renal impairment.
indications: Treatment of irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) in women younger than 65 years

dosage.d: 6 mg orally twice daily before meals
dosage.n: Take ~30 min before morning and evening meal

dosage.d: Discontinue if no response after 4-6 weeks
dosage.n: Stop if symptoms do not improve

admin: Take orally about 30 minutes before meals (twice daily)
Restricted to women under 65 without a history of cardiovascular ischemic events
Discontinue and reassess if no adequate response after 4-6 weeks
Stop immediately and seek care if cardiac symptoms (chest pain, shortness of breath) or new/worsening abdominal pain or rectal bleeding occur
moa: Tegaserod is a selective serotonin type-4 (5-HT4) receptor partial agonist. By stimulating 5-HT4 receptors in the enteric nervous system it triggers the peristaltic reflex and intestinal secretion, increases gastrointestinal motility, and reduces visceral sensitivity, thereby relieving constipation and associated symptoms in IBS-C.

absolute: History of myocardial infarction, stroke, transient ischemic attack, or angina
History of ischemic colitis or other forms of intestinal ischemia
Current or history of bowel obstruction, symptomatic gallbladder disease, suspected sphincter of Oddi dysfunction, or abdominal adhesions
Severe renal impairment or moderate-to-severe hepatic impairment
relative: Cardiovascular risk factors (e.g., hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, smoking, obesity) - assess risk
History of depression or suicidality (postmarketing reports)
monitor: New or worsening abdominal pain / rectal bleeding (ischemic colitis)

preg: There are limited human data. Animal studies did not show clear teratogenicity at clinically relevant exposures. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed and the benefit justifies the potential risk.
lact: Tegaserod and its metabolites are excreted in the milk of lactating animals (with high milk-to-plasma ratios). Because of the potential for adverse effects in the infant, avoid use or do not breastfeed during therapy.
renal: No dosage adjustment is needed in mild-to-moderate renal impairment. It is contraindicated/not recommended in severe renal impairment (end-stage renal disease).
hepatic: Use is not recommended in moderate or severe hepatic impairment and should be avoided; no adjustment data support its use in significant liver disease.

moderate: Other serotonergic agents (theoretical additive serotonergic effect)
Drugs that slow GI transit (may counteract effect)
minor: Digoxin (small decrease in digoxin Cmax/AUC observed - not usually clinically significant)
interactions.food: Taken before meals; food can reduce bioavailability so dosing is timed pre-meal

serious: Cardiovascular ischemic events (myocardial infarction, stroke, unstable angina) - basis for population restriction
Ischemic colitis and other intestinal ischemia
Severe diarrhea with hypovolemia, hypotension, or syncope
emergency: Acute cardiac ischemia (chest pain) or stroke symptoms
Ischemic colitis (severe abdominal pain, rectal bleeding)

monitoring: Symptoms of cardiovascular ischemia (chest pain, dyspnea, neurologic symptoms)
New or worsening abdominal pain or rectal bleeding (ischemic colitis)
Severity of diarrhea and hydration/blood pressure
counsel: Take about 30 minutes before your morning and evening meals
Stop the medicine and get emergency care if you have chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness on one side, trouble speaking, or severe headache
Report new or worsening stomach pain or any rectal bleeding right away - and stop the drug
If you have significant diarrhea with lightheadedness or fainting, stop and contact your doctor
Let your doctor know if you have any history of heart disease, stroke, or bowel ischemia
pk: Prokinetic effect within the first days of dosing; symptom relief over the first week
Plasma peak ~1 hour after an oral dose (taken before food)
Store at 20-25 C (controlled room temperature); protect from moisture
pearls: Withdrawn in 2007 for excess cardiovascular ischemic events; FDA reapproved (Zelnorm) in 2019 restricted to WOMEN <65 without cardiovascular ischemic history
Contraindicated with any history of MI/stroke/TIA/angina and with ischemic colitis
Bioavailability is reduced by food - dose ~30 minutes before meals
Discontinue if no response by 4-6 weeks; reassess cardiovascular risk before and during therapy
missed: If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regular time before your next meal. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Overdose may cause diarrhea, headache, abdominal pain, hypotension, and nausea/vomiting. There is no specific antidote; treatment is supportive with attention to fluid and electrolyte replacement for diarrhea-related losses. Hemodialysis has not been studied as removal therapy.
